title: OSPF Basics: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Imagine every router drawing the exact same map of the network. Then each one works out the shortest way across it. That's O S P F.

lines.t: Every router draws the same map

scenes.heading: The postal planners
scenes.narration: Think of a national postal service with a team of planners. Each planner tells everyone which cities they connect to, and how far each road is. That message is a link state advertisement. Everyone collects all the messages and builds the same complete map. Then each planner works out the cheapest path for themselves. The cost is based on how fast the road is.

scenes.heading: Turning it on
scenes.narration: Three things to remember. Start the process. Tell it which interfaces to use, with a wildcard mask. And check your neighbours. Hello packets go out every ten seconds.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three slip-ups. O S P F uses cost, not hop count. The network command takes a wildcard mask. And two way is perfectly normal between routers that are not the D R or B D R.

items.right: It uses cost, based on bandwidth

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. O S P F shares a full map, and every router finds its own best path. Cost is based on bandwidth, not hops. And the network command uses wildcard masks. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva OSPF lab.

points.t: Shared map, each router picks its path
